newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CRICKET-BANGLADESH LIFT ICC TROPHY OFF LAST BALL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BANGLADESH LIFT ICC TROPHY OFF LAST BALL.

text.p: Bangladesh survived a nail-biting finish to beat Kenya by two wickets and win the International Cricket Council (ICC) trophy World Cup qualifying tournament on Sunday.
Set a revised target of 166 in 25 overs owing to stoppages caused by rain, Bangladesh blasted 11 runs, including a six by Khaled Masud, in the last over to win off the last ball.
Bangladesh manager Gazi Ashraf was ecstatic with the win. "It was a tremendous team effort. Everyone played his part. And God was kind to us," he said.
By contrast, Kenyan manager Jasmer Singh was too disappointed to make a statement. "No comments," he said tersely.
Rain caused the final to be played over two days and Kenya had looked well placed after scoring 241 for seven in their 50 overs on Saturday with Steve Tikolo making 147.

With further overnight rain delaying the start until mid-afternoon, Bangladesh still faced a tough target from the revised total. It was made even tougher when they lost their first wicket to the very first ball of the innings.
But Bangladesh steadily made inroads on the target and were boosted Aminul Islam, with 37 from 37 balls, and Mohammed Rafique with 26 from just 15 deliveries.
With Bangladesh roared on by some 3,000 of their own nationals who work in Malaysia, they gained victory with a leg bye off the final ball of the match.
Left-arm spinner Asif Karim took three wickets but his four overs cost 31 runs. Kenyan skipper Maurice Odumbe took two for 18 off three overs.
The man of the match award went to Tikolo for his sparkling 147 for Kenya.
